description: Stack Eleven joined NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 with Novacast, a project making space and scientific data more accessible. The team was recognized as Local Event Winner. Learn more at stack-11.com.
summary: ACHA (Autonomous Crew Health Assistant) is a research and training prototype for crews that may need to act before Earth can respond. We built a web workspace to record symptoms and six health indicators, compare new measurements with a crew member’s own history, and document a repeat measurement and the outcome. In the Lunar Fatigue exercise, a crew member reports short sleep and a higher heart rate. ACHA shows the change from their baseline, flags missing context, and lets the crew link a resting repeat to the original health check. A separate onboard Python demo runs assessment rules without an Internet connection. Our research view uses NASA’s historical ISS cabin environment and radiation archives alongside clearly labeled synthetic crew scenarios. ACHA demonstrates how crews can preserve the evidence behind a decision and prepare a handover when ground support is delayed.
details:
ACHA is a research and training prototype for crews operating with delayed or intermittent support from Earth. The web workspace records heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature, sleep duration and reported symptoms. It stores timestamped records per crew member, compares observations with that person’s recent history and explains the rules used in a health check. Crew members can record a repeat, link it to the original assessment and document the outcome.

The interactive Lunar Fatigue, Orbital Pressure and Solar Relay Outage exercises let users rehearse a health check, inspect sensor gaps and follow a simulated handover. The Lunar Fatigue scenario shows why a change from a personal reference is more useful when activity and posture are known. The training replay runs offline after the app has been cached. A separate Python and SQLite onboard demo executes assessment rules locally.

We built the web app with React, TypeScript and Vite, a Python/FastAPI backend and PostgreSQL. In Research, NASA OSDR RR-6 provides archived ISS cabin temperature, humidity and CO₂. The OSDR RadLab DosTel1 archive provides historical fixed instrument radiation readings. The crew histories and scenarios are synthetic. The prototype has not undergone clinical or flight validation.
